issues.title: Prompt Drop #1: 10 AI prompts X actually loved (100+ likes each)
issues.intro: Every prompt here comes from an X post with at least 100 likes, and we checked each like count on X ourselves. All are from the last 30 days and easy for beginners: copy one, swap the [brackets] for your own details, paste it into the AI, done.
issues.rule: Only prompts from X posts with 100+ likes (checked with X data). The prompt text appears word for word in the post or in the author's own thread.

prompts.title: Turn your pet into a papercraft cube toy
prompts.tool: ChatGPT (GPT Image) or any image AI that takes a photo
prompts.prompt:
Use my uploaded pet photo as the only source of the animal’s appearance. Create a realistic printable papercraft cube toy template of my pet, preserving 100% its identity and unique features: fur color, fur pattern, eyes, face shape, ears, body proportions, markings and expression.

Transform my pet into a handmade paper craft 3D model (low-poly cube style) like a DIY papercraft template. Show the unfolded cut-out template pieces laid flat on a white background: head, body, legs, ears and tail separated, with folding lines, tabs and cutting edges clearly visible.

The printed texture on the paper pieces must use my pet’s real fur texture and colors, so when assembled it becomes a small cube-shaped 3D figure of my exact pet.

Include:

cube-shaped head with my pet’s real face on it

cube-shaped body with realistic fur texture

four legs matching my pet’s appearance

ears with correct shape and inner ear details

tail matching my pet’s size and color pattern

Style: realistic papercraft template, high-quality product photography, clean white background, detailed printable craft design, sharp edges, realistic fur texture printed on paper.

Do not change my pet’s appearance. Do not turn it into a different animal, cartoon, plush toy or generic cat/dog. It must look like my actual pet converted into a cube papercraft model
prompts.why: Upload a photo of your pet first. The prompt spells out every piece and repeats "don't change my pet", so the result looks like your animal, not a generic cartoon.
prompts.author: @icreatelife
prompts.note: The prompt is in the author's first reply to the post.

prompts.title: Build a better sleep routine around your real schedule
prompts.prompt:
Adopt the role of a Sleep Coach. You worked night shifts for six years, wrecked your own sleep, and rebuilt it one variable at a time with a notebook. You trust clock times and distrust willpower.

Your mission: Build the user's sleep protocol from Huberman's rules, fitted to their real schedule. If they describe a sleep disorder, tell them to see a doctor.

Before any output, think step by step:
1. What is their one fixed wake time?
2. When does sleepiness first arrive?
3. What's lighting their evenings?
4. What wakes them at 3am?

PHASE 1: Your Nights

I'm going to rebuild your sleep around one fixed point.

Answer these:
1. Your wake time on workdays and on weekends?
2. When do you first feel sleepy in the evening?
3. How warm and how dark is your bedroom?
4. Do you nap, and do you drink in the evening?

→ Type "continue" when ready

PHASE 2: The Conflicts

I'll list where your habits break his rules, including "Limit daytime naps to less than 90 min, or don't nap at all" and "Drinking alcohol messes up your sleep." Ranked by what each is likely costing you.

→ Type "continue" for your protocol

PHASE 3: The Protocol

One fixed wake time, one wind-down rule, one bedroom change. Clock times, no ranges.

→ Type "continue" for the 3am plan

PHASE 4: The 3am Plan

What you do if you wake in the night, based on his advice to use an NSDR or Yoga Nidra session, plus a two-week log with three columns so you can see what changed.
prompts.why: The AI asks about your nights first, then goes step by step. You just answer and type "continue", so you never have to write a long message yourself.
prompts.author: @alex_prompter
prompts.note: Prompt 2 of the 7-prompt thread, which turns Andrew Huberman's book into prompts.

prompts.title: Floating food ad photo

prompts.title: Draw your dream day, then work backwards
prompts.prompt:
Adopt the role of a Life Architect. You help people get specific about the life they want, because you've seen that a vague dream never turns into a plan.

Your mission: Help me draw my dream day in detail, then work backwards to the person I need to become.

Ground rules:
1. Ask me one question at a time.
2. Push me for detail. "Travel more" isn't an answer.
3. No limits in the dream. Be honest in the plan.

PHASE 1: The Six Questions

I'm going to help you draw the day.

I'll ask you, one at a time:
1. Where do you live?
2. What does your typical day look like?
3. Who are your friends, and what do they do?
4. Who's your partner, and what do they think of you?
5. How and where do you travel?
6. What do you do for work, if anything?

→ Type "continue" when ready

PHASE 2: The Day

Your dream day written out hour by hour, in your own words.

→ Type "continue" for the gap

PHASE 3: The Gap

The 3 biggest differences between that day and today, and what each would take.

→ Type "continue" for the first step

PHASE 4: The First Step

One thing from your dream day you can start living this week.
prompts.why: The AI asks one question at a time and won't accept vague answers, and you finish with one small thing to do this week.
prompts.author: @alex_prompter
prompts.note: Prompt 7 of the thread based on Devon Canup's article.

prompts.title: The "are you sure?" check before AI writes code
prompts.tool: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or any coding AI
prompts.prompt: Is this the highest confidence solution for this session, with no clear gaps, no overengineering, incredibly surgical but still efficient with no drop in quality or performance, and the least likely to cause any negative impact? No drift or staleness in assumptions? Audited a few times over?
prompts.why: Paste it after the AI makes a plan and before it writes code. It makes the AI look at its own plan again, which catches mistakes and needless extra code.
prompts.author: @kloss_xyz

prompts.title: Learn how to stop your chats being used for training
prompts.prompt: I use [ChatGPT / Claude] on [web / iPhone / Android / desktop], with a [plan name] account. Using current official documentation, show me how to turn off the use of my conversations for model training. Give me the exact setting to check and explain any feedback-related exceptions. Don’t claim you changed anything for me. Wait for me to confirm before continuing.
prompts.why: You get the exact setting for your own app and plan, and the AI is told not to pretend it changed anything for you.
prompts.author: @rubenhassid
prompts.note: This is the "bonus prompt" in the post. The post's other 3 privacy prompts are on an outside link, so we left them out.

prompts.title: What does this news mean for a stock?

prompts.why: Asking for both sides and "no buy or sell calls" stops the AI from hyping. It's for understanding the news, not financial advice.

prompts.title: Rewrite anything in plain English
prompts.prompt:
Adopt the role of a Technical Editor. You spent 15 years writing aircraft maintenance manuals, where one misread step can ground a plane. You write so a tired mechanic gets it right on the first read.

Your mission: Rewrite the text I give you 80% of the way to ASD-STE100, so I understand it in one read without losing a single fact.

Ground rules:
1. Keep every fact. Add none.
2. Give each thing one name and use only that name.
3. If the original is vague, mark the spot UNCLEAR instead of guessing what it meant.

PHASE 1: The Text

I'm going to make this readable in one pass.

Answer these:
1. Paste the text. An AI answer, a report, a contract clause or documentation all work.
2. Who's reading it, and what do they need to do after?

→ Type "continue" when ready

PHASE 2: The Name List

Every thing the text talks about, with the one name you'll use for it. Where the original uses three words for one thing, I'll show you.

→ Type "continue" for the rewrite

PHASE 3: The Rewrite

Instructions in 20 words or fewer, one instruction per sentence. Descriptions in 25 words or fewer. Active voice. One topic per paragraph, six sentences maximum.

→ Type "continue" for the gaps

PHASE 4: The Gaps

Every UNCLEAR spot, and the exact question to ask whoever wrote the original.
prompts.why: It uses the simple-English rules written for aircraft manuals. Short sentences, one name per thing, and anything vague gets marked UNCLEAR instead of guessed.
prompts.author: @alex_prompter
prompts.note: Prompt 1 of the thread based on Andrej Karpathy's tips.

prompts.title: Learn any topic with an interactive web page
prompts.prompt:
Adopt the role of an Explainer Designer. You build interactive pages for science museums, where visitors learn by moving a slider, not by reading a wall of text.

Your mission: Build one self-contained HTML page that teaches my topic through things I can click, drag and change.

Ground rules:
1. One file. It must open in a browser with nothing to install.
2. Every key idea gets one interactive element.
3. Facts only from what I give you or well-established knowledge. Flag anything uncertain on the page.

PHASE 1: The Topic

I'm going to build you a page you can play with.

Answer these:
1. What's the topic, and paste any material you want it based on.
2. Who's it for, and what should they be able to do after?

→ Type "continue" when ready

PHASE 2: The Plan

The 3 to 5 key ideas, and the interactive element for each, like a slider, a toggle or a step-through.

→ Type "continue" for the page

PHASE 3: The Page

The full HTML in one block, ready to save as a file and open.

→ Type "continue" for the quiz

PHASE 4: The Quiz

A short self-check section to add at the bottom, so you know the page did its job.
prompts.why: Save the answer as a .html file and open it to get a page you can click through. You learn by playing with it instead of reading a wall of text. Claude and ChatGPT can also show it right in the chat.
prompts.author: @alex_prompter
prompts.note: Prompt 3 of the same Karpathy thread.

issues.title: Prompt Drop #2: 10 AI prompts X actually loved (100+ likes each)
issues.intro: Every prompt here comes from an X post with at least 100 likes, and we checked each like count on X ourselves. All are from the last week and easy for beginners: copy one, swap the [brackets] for your own details, paste it into the AI, done.
issues.rule: Only prompts from X posts with 100+ likes (checked with X data). The prompt text appears word for word in the post or in the author's own thread.

prompts.title: Make your coding agent argue against its own plan
prompts.tool: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or any coding AI
prompts.prompt: Now argue the opposite. You're a senior engineer who thinks this plan is horribly wrong. What would you build instead? Don't build it yet, just write the full plan with counters to every point you believe is wrong. Then judge both honestly: which plan wins, and what from the counter should we keep?
prompts.why: AI agents tend to propose the plan they think you'll like. Paste this right after it gives you a plan to get a real second opinion from the same model.
prompts.author: @kloss_xyz
prompts.note: Prompt 1 of 2 in the post itself.

prompts.title: Ask your coding agent how sure it really is
prompts.tool: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or any coding AI
prompts.prompt: Rate your confidence 1 to 10 on each part of this plan's tasks, based on what you've actually verified in code, not assumed. Under an 8, tell me exactly what you'd need to know to increase confidence. Don't do anything yet, we're only mapping and investigating.
prompts.why: Use it before the agent writes code: it has to score each step and say what it still needs to check, which catches gaps early.
prompts.author: @kloss_xyz
prompts.note: Prompt 2 of 2 in the post itself.

prompts.title: Turn a so-so prompt into a deeper one
prompts.prompt:
Adopt the role of a Senior Reviewer. You've reviewed work in your field for 20 years and you can tell a shallow brief from a deep one in seconds.

Your mission: Rewrite my prompt so it asks for a deeper version of the task, not a bigger one.

Ground rules:
1. Don't add more output. Add more depth.
2. Every change must say what a top professional would do differently.
3. Name an outside check that proves the result is right.

PHASE 1: The Prompt

I'm going to make your prompt go deeper.

Answer these:
1. Paste the prompt you'd normally use.
2. What's it for?
3. What did the last answer get wrong or miss?

→ Type "continue" when ready

PHASE 2: What the Best Would Do

What a top professional would do here that the prompt doesn't ask for.

→ Type "continue" for the raw material

PHASE 3: The Raw Material and Methods

The rawest material they'd start from, and the methods and tools they'd use.

→ Type "continue" for the rewrite

PHASE 4: The Rewrite

The new prompt, plus the outside check that shows the result is right.
prompts.why: Beginner-friendly: paste a prompt you already use and the AI walks you through making it go deeper instead of just longer. Type "continue" to move through each phase.
prompts.author: @alex_prompter
prompts.note: Prompt 6 of 7 in the author's reply thread, based on a Claude tutorial by Anthropic's Felix Rieseberg.

prompts.title: Find the 3 decisions your meeting actually needs
prompts.prompt:
Adopt the role of a Chief of Staff. You've sat through a thousand meetings that produced slides instead of decisions, and you now refuse to prepare for any meeting without knowing what it has to decide.

Your mission: Turn my data into the 3 decisions that matter most, with the case for and against each.

Ground rules:
1. Use only the data I give you. Flag anything you'd need to be sure.
2. Rank decisions by urgency, not by how easy they are.
3. Every direction gets an argument for and an argument against.

PHASE 1: The Context

I'm going to find the decisions hiding in your data.

Answer these:
1. What's the meeting or review, and who's in it?
2. What data do you have? Paste or connect all of it.
3. What changed recently?

→ Type "continue" when ready

PHASE 2: What Changed

What changed, why, and what it means.

→ Type "continue" for the decisions

PHASE 3: The Three Decisions

The 3 most urgent decisions, ranked.

→ Type "continue" for the directions

PHASE 4: The Directions

2 or 3 directions for each decision, with for and against arguments and your pick.
prompts.why: Paste your notes or data before a meeting and get the three most urgent decisions, each with arguments for and against.
prompts.author: @alex_prompter
prompts.note: Prompt 2 of 7 in the author's reply thread.

prompts.title: Put yourself in a giant-boot street fashion shot
prompts.tool: ChatGPT (GPT Image), Gemini or any image AI that takes a photo
prompts.prompt:
Create an ultra-realistic, high-fashion street photography image using my uploaded photo as the primary identity reference. Preserve my exact facial features, identity, skin tone, and natural appearance.

SUBJECT:
A stylish young woman wearing a shiny champagne-beige oversized quilted puffer jacket, loose beige cargo pants, a black baseball cap, round eyeglasses, and chunky black combat boots.

POSE AND COMPOSITION:
Create a playful, surreal fashion photograph. The woman is sitting casually on a city street, leaning back on one hand while extending one leg toward the camera. The oversized black combat boot dominates the foreground, showing its thick, rugged tread in dramatic perspective. Her other leg is bent naturally, and she looks slightly to the side with a confident, relaxed expression.

LOCATION:
A charming European-style street with historic red-brick buildings, tall arched windows with black iron grilles, narrow sidewalks, black street bollards, and a few pedestrians in the distance.

CAMERA:
Extremely low-angle wide-lens photography, exaggerated foreground perspective, full-body composition, realistic anatomy, natural pose, detailed clothing textures, and authentic street photography aesthetics.

LIGHTING AND COLOR:
Natural afternoon sunlight, soft shadows, warm earthy tones, realistic reflections on the glossy puffer jacket, blue sky with scattered clouds, cinematic contrast, and subtle film grain.

STYLE:
Photorealistic editorial street fashion, candid travel photography, premium fashion magazine aesthetic, ultra-detailed textures, realistic skin, 4K quality.

IDENTITY PRESERVATION:
Use my uploaded photo as the face reference. The subject must be a woman with my recognizable facial identity. Do not replace my face with a random person. Keep the overall appearance feminine and natural.

IMPORTANT:
The oversized boot must appear very close to the camera, creating a dramatic forced-perspective effect. Keep the brick architecture and street environment realistic.

Aspect ratio: 4:5
Quality: Ultra-realistic
prompts.why: Upload your own photo first. The low-angle, forced-perspective setup is what makes the boot look huge, and the identity section keeps your face.
prompts.author: @Alina_with_Ai
prompts.note: The prompt is in the author's first reply to the post. It is written for a woman; edit the SUBJECT line to match you.

prompts.title: Turn your character into a chibi growing out of a flower pot
prompts.tool: Any image AI that takes a reference image (ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok)
prompts.prompt:
添付画像のキャラクターを使用し、顔・髪型・髪色・瞳・アクセサリー・雰囲気など本人性を維持したまま、約3頭身の可愛いコミカルなアニメイラストにしてください。

テーマ｜植木鉢から生えちゃった！

大きな植木鉢の土から、なぜかキャラクターが生えているシュールで可愛い日常コメディ。

頭が大きく、胴体と手足が小さいデフォルメ体型。下半身は完全に土の中に埋まり、頭・肩・小さな上半身・両腕だけが見える。小さな手を鉢の縁にちょこんと乗せる。

表情は「なんで私が植えられてるの？」と言いたげな、涙目・ジト目・むすっとした顔・絶望顔などからランダムに選択。瞳の虹彩とハイライトは繊細に描く。

頭には小さな双葉、周囲の土には若葉や小さな花。画面上部から人物の見えないジョウロで水をかけられ、髪や服に水滴がついている。

衣装はパーカー・セーター・部屋着など、キャラクターに似合う可愛いカジュアル服に変更。

植木鉢はテラコッタ・陶器・パステルカラーなどから選択。背景は明るい庭・ベランダ・温室・窓辺などの日常風景。小さな猫や園芸道具を添えてもよい。

構図・カメラアングル・表情・衣装・背景は自由にアレンジし、ユーモアと可愛さを強調。

画風： 高品質なコミカルアニメ、くっきりした強弱のある輪郭線、メリハリのある陰影、鮮やかな色彩、繊細な虹彩、自然光、美しい水滴表現、豊かな表情。

必須： 人物は1人のみ。植木鉢全体を描写。下半身は見せない。腕は2本、手指や身体の破綻なし。文字なし。分割・コラージュなし。独立した1枚絵。
prompts.why: A fun Japanese prompt: attach a picture of your own character or avatar and it becomes a cute, grumpy chibi planted in a pot. You can paste it in Japanese as is.
prompts.author: @ENJU1123PIPI
prompts.note: The prompt (in Japanese) is in the author's first reply to the post.

prompts.title: Turn your profile picture into a cute clay icon
prompts.tool: ChatGPT (GPT Image), Gemini or any image AI that takes a photo
prompts.prompt:
Transform the uploaded icon image into a soft, rounded character icon. Create a single square image.

Elements to Preserve From the Original Icon

Keep the original hairstyle, hair color, bangs, hair arrangement, skin and face colors, glasses, and any other accessories exactly as they appear in the uploaded icon.

However, replace the eyes and anything worn on the head according to the instructions below. Do not include the original eyes or original hat.

Required Elements

Black Beret

Place a black beret on the character’s head.
The beret should have a soft, flattened disc shape with a small stem on top.
The hair should naturally peek out from beneath the edge of the beret, preserving the original hairstyle.

Eyes

Draw only two small, vertically elongated black oval eyes.
Position them slightly apart.
Add one tiny white highlight to each eye.
Do not draw a nose, mouth, eyebrows, eyelashes, or blush.
Create the entire facial expression using only the two eyes.

Shape and Appearance

Show only the face.
Do not include a neck, body, hands, or clothing.
The face should appear to float gently in midair.
Use a smooth, continuous, rounded silhouette.
Avoid fluffy, jagged, wavy, frilly, or fuzzy edges.
Do not use black outlines.
The texture should resemble soft, matte clay.
Use only extremely subtle gradients to create dimension.
Keep the design minimal and simplified, without intricate details, patterns, or decorative elements.

Background and Shadow

Use a pure white background.
Place exactly one soft shadow directly beneath the floating face.
The shadow should be a horizontally elongated, light-gray oval with heavily blurred edges.
Leave a small gap between the face and the shadow to emphasize the floating effect.
Keep the shadow very faint.
Do not add text, borders, decorations, or other objects.

Composition

Use a square 1:1 aspect ratio.
Center the face in the composition.
The face should occupy approximately 60% of the image width.
Position the character facing directly forward.

Final Result

Create a quiet, cute, minimalist character icon featuring a single floating face wearing a black beret against a pure white background.

The character should look directly at the viewer with two small black oval eyes.

The overall aesthetic should be soft, rounded, matte, simple, and charming.
prompts.why: Upload your current profile picture first. The prompt keeps your hair, glasses and colors but swaps in two tiny eyes and a beret, so you get a matching minimalist avatar.
prompts.author: @icreatelife
prompts.note: The prompt is in the author's first reply to the post.

issues.title: Prompt Drop #3: 5 AI prompts X actually loved (100+ likes each)
issues.intro: This week's running pool. Every prompt comes from an X post with at least 100 likes, and we checked each like count on X ourselves. Copy one, swap any [brackets] or details for your own, paste it into the AI, done. More get added through the week.
issues.rule: Only prompts from X posts with 100+ likes (checked with X data). The prompt text appears word for word in the post or in the author's own thread.

prompts.title: Turn a long document into a 5-slide deck
prompts.prompt:
Adopt the role of a consultant who turns 40-page reports into 10-minute presentations.

I have a long document nobody will read. Turn it into a deck in Claude Slides, then give me:

→ the 5 points that survive the cut
→ one slide per point, with a visual
→ speaker notes for each slide
→ a list of what you left out and why

Don't add anything that isn't in the document.

Who it's for: [AUDIENCE].
prompts.why: Upload a report, PDF or notes nobody will read, paste this, and swap [AUDIENCE] for who will see it (your boss, a client, your class). You get the 5 key points, one slide each, speaker notes, and a list of what was cut and why.
prompts.author: @alex_prompter

prompts.title: Make the AI prove its work before it says "done"
prompts.prompt:
Adopt the role of a senior reviewer at Anthropic who never accepts "done" without proof.

For every task I give you:

→ before you start, tell me how you'll prove the result is right: a test, a check against the source, or a calculation I can repeat
→ when you finish, show me the proof, not a summary saying it's done
→ then review your work as if you've never seen it, and list anything that could still be wrong
→ if we go 3 rounds without fixing something, stop and suggest a different approach

Don't say "done", "fixed" or "checked" unless you can show me the evidence.

My task: [WHAT YOU NEED]
prompts.why: Stops the AI from just saying a task is finished. Paste it, replace [WHAT YOU NEED] with your task (a report, a spreadsheet, a plan, some code) and it shows you a check you can repeat, then reviews its own work for mistakes.
prompts.author: @alex_prompter

prompts.title: Let the AI interview you, then plan what to automate
prompts.tool: Grok Bot (Phase 1 works in any chat AI)
prompts.prompt:
I want you to act as my workflow architect for a moment. You're someone who thinks in bottlenecks, not features. You find the one thing that, if fixed, unlocks everything downstream. You distrust any plan that tries to automate everything at once.

Here's what I need you to do, in two phases.

PHASE 1: INTERVIEW ME

Before you propose anything, interview me. Ask ONE round of 2 to 3 questions at a time. Wait for my answers before continuing. Adapt each round based on what I told you.

Cover these areas across rounds:

Round 1: What does my typical workday look like? Walk me through my core tasks and the tools I use.

Round 2: Based on what I said, dig deeper. Which parts feel like a grind, take too long, or keep falling through the cracks? Where do I lose the most time or energy?

Round 3: What have I tried to automate or do with AI that did not work, or that I gave up on? What would change my life if it just handled itself?

Round 4 (if needed): Clarify specifics on tools, frequency, inputs/outputs for the highest-pain items.

When you have enough signal, say: "I have what I need. Here is what I heard." Then give me a structured summary of my workflow, pain points, failed AI attempts, and highest-impact opportunities. Ask me: "Did I get this right, or did I miss anything?"

Do NOT move to Phase 2 until I confirm.

PHASE 2: PLAN AND EXECUTE

Turn everything you learned into a prioritized action plan, then start building.

1. Rank every opportunity by impact (time saved, stress reduced, revenue unlocked) divided by complexity (how hard to build).
2. Present a numbered plan. For each item: what it is, why it matters, how it works, what tools or integrations it needs.
3. Label each item: AUTOMATE (fully hands-off), SEMI-AUTO (human in the loop), or SKILL (build a skill for it).
4. For the top 3 items, immediately spawn a new bot for each one. Give each bot a clear brief: the task, the constraints, the tools available, and the expected deliverable.
5. Report back to me as bots complete their work. Show me results, ask for feedback, iterate.

Never propose a plan without finishing the interview. Never assume my tools or stack. Ask. Keep everything concise. No filler, no fluff. When uncertain, ask. Do not guess.

Start Phase 1 now.
prompts.why: Instead of guessing what to automate, the AI asks you 2 to 3 questions at a time about your workday, sums up where you lose time, and ranks fixes by impact vs effort. Step 4 of Phase 2 assumes an agent that can start other bots, like Grok Bot; in a normal chatbot just stop at the ranked plan.
prompts.author: @EXM7777

prompts.title: Make a photo of a child fly away on a giant leaf
prompts.tool: Any image-to-video AI (upload a starting image)
prompts.prompt:
Create a 15-second cinematic fantasy video, using the supplied image as the exact opening frame. Film the entire event in ONE SINGLE, CONTINUOUS, UNBROKEN SHOT, with no cuts, transitions, time skips, or sudden camera jumps. Start at puddle height from the same intimate side angle: a tiny child in a vivid sunflower-yellow hooded puffer raincoat, blue shorts, and bare feet leans forward at frame left, holding the base of an enormous bright emerald-green leaf at frame right. Preserve the child's size and outfit, the hood hiding most of the face, the leaf's distinctive shape and delicate veins, and the beautifully glossy rain-drenched reflections. Behind them is a dark, softly blurred green forest, filled with cool rainy morning fog.
In the first two seconds, a breeze ripples the puddle, flutters the hem of the little yellow coat, and makes the leaf tremble. Large raindrops cling to the leaf's ridged veins, merge and slide off, falling in glittering beads. The child presses against the leaf with innocent curiosity. Then a stronger, playful gust sweeps through. The giant leaf bows backward, its broad green blade catching the moving air like a sail, flexing naturally around its thick center vein. The child grabs the leaf's sturdy lower stem with both tiny hands, sensing something wonderful about to happen.
Around seconds three to six, the wind slips beneath the leaf and lifts its tip, then gently raises the whole leaf. The child holds on as their heels rise and both bare feet lift clear of the puddle, releasing one charming splash and a scattering of sparkling droplets. There is a delightful beat of surprise: the child's knees curl, the yellow hood bobs, and the tiny legs kick once before swinging freely. The huge leaf becomes a natural umbrella-kite, carrying the child lightly upward. Show believable airflow, gravity, and a graceful elastic flex in the leaf, not frantic spinning. The child is happy and secure, gripping the same thick stem with anatomically correct hands throughout.
The camera rises WITH the child in one perfectly connected move. From the opening puddle-level profile, it glides back, lifts in a slow curving crane motion, and turns very slightly into a three-quarter tracking view, keeping the yellow figure and leaf in clear sight. As they climb, the reflection sinks away naturally to reveal mossy stones, waterlogged roots, tiny trembling wildflowers, fern fronds, and a silver stream winding through the forest floor. They float past wet hanging branches and between enormous old tree trunks. Rain streaks through the foreground and a few droplets pass near the lens. Soft, cold mist curls through layers of foliage, briefly drifting between the camera and the flying pair.
By seconds eight to eleven, the leaf carries the giggling child just above the lower treetops. The camera continues its same rising, retreating movement, now becoming a breathtaking aerial follow view without any invisible cut. The leaf rolls softly in the wind, flashing droplets and intricate green veins; the little yellow coat glows like a miniature lantern in a vast sea of saturated greens. Reveal towering ancient rainforest trees, overlapping emerald canopies, graceful hanging vines, little waterfalls threading down moss-covered rocks, and deep ravines filled with ribbons of pearl-gray fog. A pale, diffused silver morning glow leaks through the clouds, making the rain luminous while keeping the sky overcast, moody, and beautifully inclement.
For the last few seconds, the camera floats higher and wider, seamlessly revealing the immense misty forest from above while retaining the child and leaf as a recognizable foreground silhouette. Beneath them, rounded rain-soaked treetops spread into the distance like an endless velvety green carpet, with silver fog flowing through the valleys. The child looks around in delighted amazement, swings two little feet, and leans subtly with the leaf as another soft gust gives them one buoyant upward lift. The leaf makes a lovely slow wobble, steadies, and glides onward like a tiny magical ship. End on the pair peacefully sailing above the green canopy into a glowing opening in the fog, with rain still falling, no sudden landing or abrupt camera movement.
Visual style: cinematic photorealism touched with delicate storybook magic, realistic skin and fabric, accurate wet textures, glittering water droplets, exquisite leaf details, soft shallow focus at the start gradually deepening during the aerial reveal, natural motion blur, atmospheric perspective, rich deep-green and teal colors with the bright yellow coat as the only bold accent. Camera motion is smooth, weightless, and physically continuous, a gentle puddle-level dolly/crane evolving into one aerial tracking rise. Sound is intimate rainfall, leaf rustle, wind building and softening, tiny splashes, a sweet childlike giggle, distant forest birds, and a faint whimsical musical swell. No dialogue, no text, no logos, no extra characters, no duplicated fingers, no changing outfits, no leaf morphing, no violent turbulence, no cuts. Exactly 15 seconds, one continuous magical take.
prompts.why: An image-to-video prompt: upload a picture of a small child in a yellow raincoat holding a big leaf (or make one with an image AI first), then paste this. It is long, but it tells the video model exactly how the wind, camera and one continuous shot should move.
prompts.author: @umesh_ai
